passage.text: A large amount of food is thrown away by restaurants and shops every day. Some smartphone apps let shops sell food that has not been sold at a lower price. Shops take photos of such food and put them on the app before closing time. In this way, they reduce waste and earn money at the same time. These apps have become popular among young people.

The next week, she was taking photos of the bread and putting them on an app. That evening, several young customers were buying the bread at a lower price. questions.prompt: Some people say that shops should be fined for throwing away food that can still be eaten. What do you think about that?
questions.modelAnswer: I disagree. Shops throw food away because they are afraid of making customers sick. A fine would only make them order less and lose sales. Support for donating the food would work better.

questions.prompt: Today, many people care about environmental problems. Do you think young people can change society?

yes.modelAnswer: Young people spread ideas quickly online, and companies change their products to match what they want.

no.modelAnswer: Young people have little money and few votes. Real change needs the people who make the rules.
